note: Combined stats blend six registers and understate engineering prose. When rewriting, use the matching entry in 'registers', not the top-level numbers. Sources: 4 PR descriptions, 11 Jira tickets/comments (3 too short for the indexer, so jira stats cover 8), 34 Mattermost messages in 3 files, 6 technical design/spec docs (template headers and code stripped, 9,760 words), 3 fiction pieces, 8 talk scripts (2 are excerpts). Talks contain scripture quotes, which are not the author's voice. Built 2026-10-30 with voice-indexer.py plus a merge step. Work-domain word lists, coworker names and internal system names were removed before publishing.

markers: spaced hyphen ' - ' as a dash, never an em dash
slash alternatives: updated/changed, frozen screen/black screen
parenthetical asides for rationale or config detail
very long sentences chained with 'and', 'since', 'so'; short sentences land as flat conclusions
casual intensifiers in informal openers: 'Yep', 'waaayyy too much'
plain verbs: is/are/has, 'gets destroyed', 'goes to the same queue'
exact identifiers verbatim (class names, config flags with their values), links to upstream issues/docs
problem first, then mechanism, then why it works
'Note that' for caveats; no hedging otherwise
lowercase product names mid-sentence; sloppy spacing (double spaces after periods, space before final period after URL)
no bold, no emoji, no headers, no sign-offs or closers
short, often 1-3 sentence tickets; problem or current behavior first, then the change ('Right now...', 'Currently...', 'When we send...')
'This is because...' / 'This is needed so that...' to give the cause, then 'Ideally we'd...' or 'We should...' for the ask
'We' for the team and the system; imperative for the task ('Replace...', 'Setup...', 'Added...')
lowercase informal fragments and shorthand are fine; occasional all-caps for a follow-up note
class, bean, setting, and service names verbatim; real values stated (a concurrency limit, a library version, a date)
spaced hyphen ' - ' for asides; parentheses for rationale
scope and priority stated plainly ('Not critical for Thursday as long as we don't re-deploy', 'Smoke testing ... will be sufficient')
direct questions to named people at the end ('<name> <name> do you agree?')
unpunctuated list lines for task lists, no bullets or bold
jira.caution: Two samples contain spaced em dashes. They read like AI-assisted drafts, so the em-dash count here may not be the author's own habit. The confirmed dash in this register is ' - '.

chat.stat_caveat: sentence_length is recomputed with message boundaries as sentence breaks, because the indexer merges messages that lack final punctuation.
markers: one thought per message, usually under 20 words; a single message can be a lone line
about 40% start lowercase and skip the final period; announcements and longer posts use full capitalization and punctuation
'i' lowercase in quick replies, 'I' in longer ones; 'I' is the most common opener
ellipses in speech-like asides
questions to the room, often tentative
softened pushback with a stated reason ('having that change spread between two files is brittle. If there's not a simple way it's fine.')
casual humor and emoji sparingly (':)', a laughing emoji); no sign-offs
parenthetical asides with a wry note ('(and hopefully tokens get cheaper? Maybe? Probably not)')
announcements: say what is available, how to get it, how to invoke it, then what feedback is wanted, in short lines
plain statement of own state when relevant ('It was a stressful morning')
tags people with @Name and gives the exact value they need

specs.stat_caveat: PDF extraction leaves some bullet lists and signature lines merged into long units, so the mean is inflated. Trust the median (20) and P75 (32).
markers: Summary opens on the current state ('Currently X is done by Y'), then the pain ('This is an extra step... very error prone'), then the alternative ('An alternative that provides...')
design statements in plain active voice: 'we accept batches', 'To avoid overload...', 'To avoid abuse, rules will be setup'
best-practice docs address the reader directly with a blunt rule plus the reason ('In general, don't use X for Y, this is what Z is for.')
'In general' to state a default, 'Note that' for a caveat, 'At the very least skim...' for a minimum bar
back-of-envelope math written inline with honest hedges ('ballpark handwavy figure', 'let's round up', '1.5x safety buffer', 'Plenty of room to grow')
terminology sections define terms in one short line ('Node: slab of memory running the engine')
short phrase bullets under a heading, not full sentences; exact destinations, class names, and config keys verbatim
section order is fixed by the template (Summary, Technical Design, Dependencies, Test Strategy, Impact & Risk, Scalability); the prose under each is brief
parentheticals for rationale and examples ('(there are libraries for that)', 'e.g. when keys need to be cycled/updated')
slash alternatives and informal verbs survive in formal docs ('cycled/updated', 'stashed to config server')
no em dashes, no bold in running text, no closing recap
avoid: formal filler ('it should be noted that')
specs.caution: Header blocks, TOCs, jira macros, links, and meeting passcodes were stripped before indexing. Co-authored docs (other developers listed) may not be solely your wording.

markers: short declarative sentences, many fragments as punch ('Not yet.', 'It was her body.', 'The graph reached critical levels.')
refrain/callback lines repeated with one detail changed ('The lighting on the operations floor was...')
ordinal noticing: 'The first thing she noticed... The second thing she noticed...'
dashes as asides: spaced ' - ' and spaced em dash ' — ' both appear
concrete numbers and objects (11,000 times per second, rivets, coffee mugs, token stick)
understatement and hedged narration ('Hesitation first. Then resignation, sort of.', 'might be described as')
'Somehow,' and 'A beat.' as transitions; dialogue clipped, no tags beyond 'said' or an action
worldbuilding via invented nouns used without explanation (Corp-Sec, vidcams, Cobalts, token exchange stick)
avoid: tidy summing-up lines after a scene beat

markers: spoken, second-person and 'we' address; rhetorical questions answered right away ('Did that rub off?', 'Have those words proven true? Absolutely.')
'Yes,' as an affirming opener; also 'Sadly,', 'No doubt', 'Of course', 'Notice', 'Now then,', 'So,'
everyday analogies carry the point (leaky roof, anchor, driving a car, Jack in the Box); concrete over abstract
scripture inline after a spaced hyphen, with (READ) cues as stage directions
contrast structure: 'Contrast this with...', 'Now compare that situation with...'
long sentences with comma-chained clauses; short punch sentence after ('Lives saved.', 'You won't find it.')
plain vocabulary with occasional formal word ('fealty', 'egregious', 'entreaty')
specific stats cited with source links on outline drafts
avoid: removing the (READ) cues and time marks in outlines

cross_register: spaced hyphen ' - ' is the default dash in every register; spaced em dash appears in fiction and a few talks
starts sentences with And, But, So freely; 'and' is by far the top connector
plain verbs and concrete detail; no bold or headers in prose; emoji only in rare chat jokes
no closing-summary sentences in PRs, Jira, chat, and fiction; talks end on an exhortation, not a recap
tech, Jira, and chat give the cause with 'since', 'because', or 'This is because'
typos and uneven spacing are left in (double spaces, 'your hearts desire'); do not 'fix' them unless asked
qualitative.pronoun_use: tech and Jira: impersonal or 'we', occasional 'I'; chat: first person 'I' dominant; specs: impersonal with 'we', imperative for guidance; fiction: close third; talks: 'we' and 'you'
